name: Ruins of Thaurissan
summary: Ash lies over the Ruins of Thaurissan in the Burning Steppes. The city once stood in the northern Redridge Mountains as the Dark Iron clan’s surface capital. During the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan called Ragnaros the Firelord, and the eruption reduced the city to cinders.

sections.title: The Fall of a Kingdom
sections.body:
After High King Modimus Anvilmar died, the Dark Iron clan was exiled from Ironforge. Roughly two centuries ago, they traveled south and founded Thaurissan City. During the War of the Three Hammers, the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans joined forces and brought the Dark Iron to the edge of defeat.

Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan sought a weapon to turn the tide. He and seven trusted sorcerers worked ancient magic deep beneath the earth. Their ritual did not summon an obedient servant. It tore open a path to the Elemental Plane and brought forth Ragnaros the Firelord. The eruption shattered the surrounding mountains, scorched the land into the Burning Steppes, raised Blackrock Mountain, and incinerated the city.

sections.title: Echoes in the Ash
sections.body:
Shattered masonry and crumbled pillars lie across the wasteland. Dark Iron remnants patrol among fire elementals. The Alliance has sent expeditions to recover relics buried beneath the ash, guided by Royal Historian Archesonus in Ironforge.

Touching the enchanted remnants brings vivid, terrifying memories of the cataclysm: eight dwarves chanting in despair, seven corpses sprawled around a lone kneeling thaumaturge, and a towering monolith of primal flame. That flame claimed an entire clan’s souls and freedom.

faq.q: What was this city before it was destroyed?
faq.answer: Before its destruction, Thaurissan City was the Dark Iron clan’s proud surface capital. They built it after exile from Ironforge, which followed the death of High King Modimus Anvilmar. The city became the center of their growing kingdom.

Facing defeat in the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan tried to summon a powerful supernatural minion. His ritual called Ragnaros the Firelord from beneath the earth. The Firelord’s arrival raised an apocalyptic volcano that reduced the city and surrounding valleys to charred ruins.

faq.q: Why is the ground around the ruins an ashen wasteland?
aliases: what happened to the land here
faq.answer: The land was once the fertile northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains. Ragnaros’s summoning ruptured the earth, raised Blackrock Mountain, and scorched the expanse into an ashen wasteland.

faq.q: Where did the surviving Dark Iron dwarves go?
aliases: where are the dark irons now
faq.answer: Ragnaros and his elemental minions enslaved the surviving Dark Iron dwarves. They went deep beneath Blackrock Mountain to build Shadowforge City. Their ruined capital lay behind as they toiled in service to the Firelord.

angles.text: For dwarves of Ironforge, these ruins recall the Dark Iron clan’s hubris during the War of the Three Hammers. They remember the terrible price of calling upon elemental powers.
Alliance scouts and researchers, sent by Royal Historian Archesonus of Ironforge, search the ruined foundations for relics. They seek the truth about Blackrock Mountain’s master.
